1.point: The line we hear every Thursday in Du'a Kumayl asks for one of the two things 'irfan seeks; this chapter will show we already know these words.
steps: Identify the quoted line: where it comes from, when we say it, what it asks (a heart enthralled by God's love).
Link that request to the goal of 'irfan (love of God, with knowing God as the second half).
State the chapter's claim: we already know these words.

2.point: Before anything else the prayers ask to be cut off from everything but God, and that cutting-off is in the heart, not in outward life.
steps: Show that in the Munajat Sha'baniyyah the request for severance comes before the request for sight (it is the first request).
Raise the literal reading (leave family, work, society) and give the Sheikh's answer: in the heart.
Show from the prayers' own words that what is cut away is love of the world in the heart (Abu Hamza), and that God makes this severance in the hearts of those He loves ('Arafah).
Conclude: the severance is in the heart.

3.point: After severance the prayers ask for the three things 'irfan seeks: to see God with the heart, to love Him, to be near Him.
steps: A heart cleared of all else is free for God; the prayers then make three requests.

Sight: the Munajat asks for the eyes of the heart to be lit; meet the Qur'anic objection that sight cannot perceive God by showing the prayer means the inner faculty, the light God gives a purified heart.
Love: the Munajat asks for a place among God's friends and defines that place by love; the Sheikh reads this friendship as knowing plus love, the two things 'irfan seeks.
Nearness: the Munajat asks for a heart whose passion brings it near.
Conclude: with these three the prayers have asked for all 'irfan seeks.

4.point: Although these words come from the highest level, an ordinary believer may still say them: as an honour granted, and as a plea from need, which claims no level.
steps: State the difficulty: words from the peak of understanding are given to ordinary believers to recite (primary school boy, university books).
Show that the prayers themselves speak from need and claim nothing ('Arafah; the Munajat line where even the turning to God is God's doing).
Give the Sheikh's answer: we are honoured to be allowed to recite them.
Join the two: pleas from need claim no level, so a sincere reciter may say them without grasping all their meaning, and God may grant them.

5.point: The prayers are assigned to nights and days ordinary believers already keep, so anyone may begin them, even though few comprehend all they describe.
steps: The prayers reach us through the Mafatih, which sets each on a time in the believer's year.
Give the times: the Munajat in Sha'ban; Kumayl, 'Arafah and Abu Hamza on their nights and days.
Said on kept nights, the words become familiar (Khomeini could assume this).
Meet the objection that reciting is not comprehending (Maliki Tabrizi).
Resolve: that is a different question; the claim here is only that anyone may begin, with access to the words rather than attainment.

6.point: Because the prayers ask for what 'irfan seeks, from need, on nights we keep, the goal of 'irfan is already on our lips: we have already begun to ask for it.
steps: Gather the three results: the prayers ask for 'irfan's goal, in a voice of need, on nights we keep.
Draw the conclusion: the goal is not foreign; in saying these prayers we have begun to ask for it.

¶1.label: advance
¶1.why: Identifies the displayed quotation (Du'a Kumayl, Thursday evenings) and what it asks for; the hook the opening needs.

¶2.label: advance
¶2.why: Ties the line to the two aims of 'irfan and states the chapter's claim in one sentence.

¶3.label: advance
¶3.why: Establishes that severance is the Munajat's first request, before sight; the Sheikh's remark confirms the order.

¶4.label: advance
¶4.why: Raises the literal objection (leave family, work) and gives the Sheikh's answer, 'in the heart'; introduces the Abu Hamza quotation that will show what is cut away.

¶5.label: support
¶5.why: Reads the Abu Hamza quotation (love of the world leaves the heart) and sets up 'Arafah, which says God makes the same severance in the hearts of those He loves; evidence ¶6 draws on.

¶6.label: restate
¶6.why: Its claim, that the severance is in the heart, was already made in ¶4 ('in the heart yes'); this summarises ¶5 and states the conclusion a second time.

¶7.label: advance
¶7.why: Supplies the hinge from severance to the three requests and names them; the frame the rest of the section fills.

¶8.label: advance
¶8.why: Supplies the first request (sight) and the real objection to it (the Qur'an says sight cannot perceive God), which ¶9 answers.

¶9.label: advance
¶9.why: Resolves the objection: the eyes of the heart are the inner faculty, the light God gives a purified heart; links to 'Arafah's line that God has lit it in His friends.

¶10.label: advance
¶10.why: Supplies the second request (love) and the fact that the Munajat defines friendship with God by love.

¶11.label: advance
¶11.why: Supplies the step that ties the request for friendship to 'irfan's two aims (knowing and love) through the Sheikh's reading of wilaya.

¶12.label: advance
¶12.why: Supplies the third request (nearness) and locates it in the Munajat.

¶13.label: support
¶13.why: Its first sentence reads the Munajat quotation (a heart whose passion brings it near is itself asked of God), which the step needs. The Whispered Prayer of the Lovers is a second prayer saying the same thing and could be cut without loss.

¶14.label: restate
¶14.why: The closing sentence repeats ¶7 and the section point; the sketch of how nearness feels in prayer is not used by any step and nothing later depends on it.

¶15.label: advance
¶15.why: States the difficulty the section must answer: words from the peak given to ordinary believers (the schoolboy and the university books).

¶16.label: advance
¶16.why: Supplies the first half of the answer: the prayers speak from need; introduces the 'Arafah quotation that shows it.

¶17.label: support
¶17.why: Reads the 'Arafah line (need is the only plea) and adds the Munajat line where even the turning to God is His doing; evidence for ¶18's 'they claim no level', though the second witness could be shorter.

¶18.label: advance
¶18.why: Supplies the Sheikh's answer (an honour), joins it to the plea-from-need, and draws the section's conclusion once.

¶19.label: advance
¶19.why: Supplies the step that the prayers reach us through the Mafatih, which assigns each a time in the year.

¶20.label: support
¶20.why: Gives the Munajat's time (Sha'ban) and the Mafatih's advice, the instance ¶19's claim and ¶22's 'nights we keep' rest on; the Appendix sentence is housekeeping.

¶21.label: support
¶21.why: Gives the times of the other three prayers so that 'these prayers' in the point is covered; Kumayl's and Abu Hamza's times were already given in ¶1 and ¶4, so it could be shorter.

¶22.label: advance
¶22.why: Supplies the inference from kept nights to familiar words, with Khomeini's remark as evidence that this familiarity can be assumed.

¶23.label: advance
¶23.why: Raises the objection that reciting is not comprehending (Maliki Tabrizi); the point needs it met, and ¶24 meets it.

¶24.label: advance
¶24.why: Resolves the objection by separating how far a reciter reaches from who may begin, and states the section's claim with its limit.

¶25.label: advance
¶25.why: Gathers the three earlier results and draws the chapter's conclusion; this is the section's point, stated here once.

¶26.label: aside
¶26.why: A bridge to the next chapter that raises a question this chapter does not answer; the point needs nothing from it.
